rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı treats îkān, istîkān, teyakkun, and yaqīn as synonyms; yaqīn is settled, decisive belief that matches reality and cannot be removed by doubt, or exact knowledge with no possibility of refutation.
rows.anchor: Yakīn vâkı‘a mutâbık ve herhangi bir teşkik ile zâil olmayacak surette şekk ü şüpheden ârî olan sâbit ve câzim bir itikad demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All three senses count as yaqīn, but Elmalılı reserves true yaqīn for the second and third: certainty that persists into the future or makes any alternative impossible.
rows.anchor: denilir. Fakat asıl yakīn ikinci ile üçüncüdür.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine knowledge is not called yaqīn: God's names and attributes are given by revelation, Scripture and Sunna do not use this label for His knowledge, and yaqīn is used of beings capable of doubt.
rows.anchor: İlm-i ilâhîye “yakīn” ıtlâk edilmez. Bunun iki sebebi vardır. Birincisi esmâ ve sıfât-ı ilâhiye tevkīfîdir.

rows.speaker: zâhib olanlar
rows.claim: Some scholars even hold that necessary, presential, self-evident first principles should not be called yaqīn, since the term concerns those for whom doubt is possible.
rows.anchor: yakīn ve îkān şekk ü şüphe şânından olanlar hakkında kullanılır. Bunun için ulûm-i zarûriyeye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Certainty requires correspondence with fact and absence of doubt, not that the fact be necessary; observation, experiment, mass-transmitted reports, and sound inference can yield it.
rows.anchor: Yakīnde matlub olan vâkı‘a mutabakat ve ‘adem-i reybdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Certainty has degrees: mathematics and logical deductions are necessary, while ordinary empirical sciences such as chemistry and physics can be certain without being necessary.
rows.anchor: Yakīnin merâtibi vardır. Meselâ riyaziyyât, istintâcât-ı mantıkiye yakīnî ve zarûrî olduğu gibi, ulûm-i âdiye ve mücerrebe

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Theories and hypotheses derived by faulty inference from experiments are not all certain; biology, medicine, and related fields are not yet certain knowledge.
rows.anchor: Ancak bunların vâkı‘ât-ı mücerrebesinden istidlâlât-ı fâside ile intac edilen nazariyyât ve faraziyyâtın hepsi yakīnî değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans can build aircraft but not grass, insects, or a sparrow's feather; this does not make such creation impossible, since God creates directly, through materials and seeds, or through human hands.
rows.anchor: tayyareleri yaparız, fakat bir çimeni, bir böceği, serçenin bir tüyünü yapamayız. Acaba mümkin değil midir? Mümkin olmasa idi vücûda gelmezdi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an reports prophetic examples of creating a bird from clay by God's leave, showing that natural sciences should not narrow belief in divine power or what is intrinsically possible.
rows.anchor: Nitekim peygamberlerin ellerinde yapabileceğine dair numuneler de gösterdiğini Kur’an haber de veriyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Natural sciences should strengthen and widen confidence in God's power and the range of intrinsic possibility, rather than undermine either.
rows.anchor: ulûm ve fünûn-ı tabî‘iye bizim kudretullah hakkındaki yakīnimizi ve imkân-ı zâtî husûsundaki vüs‘at-i îmânımızı yıkacak değil, takviye edip tevsî‘edecek delâil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Science should advance within its bounds; it must not be treated as exhausting God's power or both worlds, and ordinary certainties should not be sacrificed to necessary ones.
rows.anchor: Fenleri kendi hududları dâhilinde tâkip ve terakki ettirmeliyiz. Fakat onlara inanırken hiçbir zaman kudretullâhı tükettik

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God's knowledge and power predate the present witnessed world, the unseen future will also exist; what is absent or unbelievable today may come tomorrow.
rows.anchor: Bugün olmayanlar yarın olur. Bugün inanmadıklarımıza yarın inanmak mecburiyetinde kalırız.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miracles such as life from the dead, ascent to heaven, questioning in the grave, and resurrection are possible by God's leave, while logical contradictions and a human being's own independent divinity are impossible.
rows.anchor: Lâkin iki kere iki tek olur mu olmaz. Cüz küllünden büyük olur mu olmaz. Ma‘lul illetini geçer mi geçmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if a person makes a bird or raises the dead by God's permission, that person remains a servant; all possibilities lie within God's power, and the future is infinite.
rows.anchor: O Allah’ın izniyle kuş da yapsa, ölüleri de diriltse yine kuldur, yine kuldur. Bütün imkânlar kudretullahtadır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad was sent to teach comprehensive faith, the creed of divine oneness, and righteous action; those who believe in him are never deceived and remain people of certainty.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Muhammed bize mutlak olan bu îmân-ı küllîyi, bu akīde-i tevhîdi ve buna göre amel-i sâlihi tâlim için ba‘s buyurulmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ulaika is a plural demonstrative, plural of dhā; its address suffix can first address the Prophet specifically and then extend to a general address.
rows.anchor: {اُو۬لٰٓئِكَ} اُولاَءِ ism-i işâret-i cemi‘

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ulaika points to the people whose qualities the Prophet has heard or seen described: the muttaqīn who believe in all domains of faith and fulfill bodily and financial worship.
rows.anchor: “Sana söylerim bunlar, o gördüklerin, o evsâfını işittiklerin” demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those people are candidates for, and are already walking at their respective levels in, guidance from their one Lord; they hear instructive guidance and attain active guidance.
rows.anchor: O’nun hidâyetine namzet ve o hidâyet üzere

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who say or will say, Guide us to the straight path, are the ones who receive God's verbal and practical answer and succeed in walking it.
rows.anchor: اِهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَق۪يمَ diyecek olan veya diyenler bunlardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The truly and eternally successful, secure from wrath and error and reaching God's everlasting favors, are those guided by Him.
rows.anchor: cidden ve ebediyen felah bulanlar, bulacak olanlar, gazab u dalâlden sâlim olarak ni‘am-ı ebediyye-i ilâhiyeye erecekleri muhakkak olanlar ancak bunlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ultimate salvation does not belong to prophet-deniers or merely those who affirm earlier prophets; believers who neglect bodily and financial worship and righteous deeds remain in danger and lack complete salvation.
rows.anchor: İman edip bedenen ve mâlen ibadet ve a‘mâl-i sâliha yapmayanların hâlleri de tehlikeden sâlim değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such believers may still be saved by divine mercy, extraordinarily rather than by God's usual order; they must not despair, because even an atom of faith is not lost with God.
rows.anchor: Zira ‘indallah zerre-i îmân da zâyi‘olmaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muflih means one who attains falāḥ; falāḥ is linked to splitting through an obstacle, escaping it, reaching one's aim, and winning, as believers overcome worldly and sensual barriers for the unseen and eternal afterlife.
rows.anchor: “Müflih”, “iflâh”dan felah bulan demektir. Felah aslında “felâhat” gibi yarmak mânasıyla alâkadardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabic definite article in al-mufliḥūn conveys restriction; the pronoun hum is a separating pronoun that distinguishes predicate from attribute and reinforces the ruling.
rows.anchor: olursa kasr ifade eder. Burada هُم zamîr-i fasl denilen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definition can identify an already famed but unspecified group of successful people, or tell readers who did not know the term to examine its reality and recognize these people as the true ones.
rows.anchor: Birisi öteden beri müflihûn vasfıyla şöhret-şi‘âr birtakım zevât-ı mübheme vardır bunu duyarsınız, fakat tâyin edemezsiniz.

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Some interpreters say repeating ulaika marks guidance and success as separate qualities, while the waw signals that they differ in meaning and aim.
rows.anchor: tekrarı hidâyet ile felâhın müstakil birer haslet olduklarına işarettir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı prefers taking the first ulaika as the believing muttaqīn and the second as referring back to them after the guidance clause, avoiding a meaningful repetition.
rows.anchor: birinci اُو۬لٰٓئِكَ o imanları yapan müttakīlere, ikinci de عَلٰى هُدًى مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ kaydından sonra onlara râci‘olması

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance is not restricted to the muttaqīn, but success is restricted to those who have guidance.
rows.anchor: Görülüyor ki hidâyetin müttakīlere kasrı yoktur ve lâkin felâhın hidâyettekilere kasrı vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Success following guidance and guidance following piety are customary sequences, not causal necessities; God's grace and mercy are the true effective agent.
rows.anchor: felâhın hidâyete, hidâyetin takvaya terettübü de illiyet tarîkiyle değil, âdet tarîkiyle cereyân ettiğine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse connects Fātiḥa's Lord of the worlds, the covenant of You alone we worship, guidance for the muttaqīn at the sūra's opening, and the combined purpose of the three stories and rainstorm parable.
rows.anchor: Bu âyetin, Fâtiha’daki لِرَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ vasfının isbâtına, اِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ mîsâkına

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Qur'anic order this is God's first explicit command and begins Islam's foundation with the oneness of worship and lordship.
rows.anchor: Tertîb-i Kur’ân’a nazaran bu âyet Allah teâlâ’nın sarih olarak ilk emrini hâvî oluyor ki bu emir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command shows that divinity depends on lordship, lordship on creatorship, and thereby establishes God as Creator.
rows.anchor: ulûhiyetin rubûbiyete, rubûbiyetin hâlıkıyete tevakkufunu gösteriyor ve hâlıkı isbat ediyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument then establishes prophethood and defends Muhammad's truthfulness.
rows.anchor: Ve akabinde nübüvveti ve sıdk-ı Muhammedîyi isbat ve müdafaa ediyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address includes all people who have reached human maturity through reason and puberty: believers, unbelievers, hypocrites, every nation, rich and poor, learned and ignorant.
rows.anchor: hepiniz mü’min, kâfir, münafık, hangi sınıfa

words: ٱعْبُدُوا۟ رَبَّكُمُ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَكُمْ وَٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone is always obliged to worship and obey the Lord who created them and all their forebears, bowing to Him with complete love, reverent fear, respect, and good manners.
rows.anchor: Sizi ve sizden evvelkileri, babalarınızı, analarınızı, bütün atalarınızı, ecdâdınızı vesâirlerini baştan nihâyete halk eden Rabbinize

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who pledged You alone we worship should fulfill that pledge; those who did not should make it and worship and obey God.
rows.anchor: îfa etsin, vermeyenler vermeye çalışsın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The aim is that people may actually be protected and become true muttaqīn; fear of worldly events or death, or refusing to hear, cannot protect them.
rows.anchor: bilfiil korunabilesiniz, hakīkī müttakīlerden olmanızı ümit edebilesiniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La'allakum expresses hope rather than a guarantee: protection is a strong hope, not something worshippers can be certain of.
rows.anchor: Dikkat ediniz, لَعَلَّكُمْ buyuruluyor. Bu ise ümit ifade eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's will cannot be constrained by worship; servitude works by the ordinary order, while actual protection comes from divine grace and mercy.
rows.anchor: Çünkü irâde-i ilâhiyeyi hiçbir şey takyid edemez. Siz ibadetinizle O’nu korumaya mecbur edemezsiniz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship is gratitude for creation and nurture, not a power that obligates God or puts Him in anyone's debt; no one can fully render the worship and thanks God deserves.
rows.anchor: İbadet evvelemirde hilkatinizin, terbiyenizin bir şükrânıdır; bunun Allah’ı mecbur edecek, minnet altında bırakacak bir kudret-i mûcibesi yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worshippers should remain hopeful rather than assume every outcome is guaranteed, place their hope only in God, and recognize their Creator by reflecting on their creation and upbringing.
rows.anchor: ancak ümidvâr olunuz ve ümidinizi Allah’tan başkasına bağlamayınız ve Allah’ı tanımak için hilkatinize ve terbiyenize bakınız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the earth a bed: He created and raised people there and provided the conditions for their comfort, rest, waking, and everyday life.
rows.anchor: şu altınızdaki arzı size bir döşek yapmış, sizi orada yaratmış, yetiştirmiş, üzerinde her türlü rahatınız esbâbını temin etmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the earth were taken from beneath people, even their elaborate beds and palaces would be useless; rich and poor share the same earthly bed and dwelling.
rows.anchor: o altınızdan alınıvermiş olsa nerede karar ederdiniz? Kâşânelere yığdığınız kaba döşekler neye yarardı?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the decorated vault of heaven a vast, magnificent building containing the earthly bed, so all people live in one house and lie on one bed under the same Lord.
rows.anchor: başınız üstündeki müzeyyen gök kubbeyi de bu döşeği ihtivâ eden büyük muhteşem bir bina yapmış.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording presents heaven as encompassing earth, with earth like a bed inside a building; 21:32's description of heaven as a protected roof is another aspect, not a reason to read this building as merely a roof.
rows.anchor: buyurulmuş olması burada binanın sakf ile tefsîrini îcab etmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit مِنَ ٱلسَّمَاءِ rather than the pronoun مِنْهُ signals that the intended heaven is not the previously mentioned one.
rows.anchor: Burada zamir ile مِنْهُ demek lâzım gelirken zâhir olarak مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ buyurulması, bundan murad evvelki semâ olmadığına işarettir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anything above something is its samāʾ; even the ceiling of a house can be called samāʾ, so this refers to water descending from above, from clouds in the sky's direction.
rows.anchor: Zira herhangi bir şeyin fevkinde olan şey altındakinin semâsıdır. Hatta evin tavanına bile “semâ” denilir.

words: وَأَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءًۭ فَأَخْرَجَ بِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sends water from clouds and, through it, brings people sustenance from fruits and crops.
rows.anchor: de bu su sebebiyle size türlü meyvelerden, mahsullerden rızık çıkarmaktadır

words: فَأَخْرَجَ بِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ رِزْقًۭا لَّكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People drink this water and receive their share of the fruits, grains, and other produce it enables to grow while they live on earth under heaven.
rows.anchor: bu sudan içer ve bu sayede yetişen meyvelerden, hubûbât ve sâir fevâkihten kısmetlenirsiniz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These familiar signs are already known to people and require no further reading or deep philosophy; they show what a merciful Lord their Lord is.
rows.anchor: Siz bu saydıklarımızı hep bilirsiniz, bunları bilmek için başkaca okumaya veya derin felsefeler yapmaya hiç de lüzum yoktur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since people know these signs and know that none besides the Creator can be God, they must not invent equals or partners for the one true object of worship, but worship the unpartnered Creator and Lord.
rows.anchor: siz bunları ve hâlıktan başka Allah olamayacağını

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Andād is the plural of nidd and has the same meaning as mithl and amthāl: a likeness or equal.
rows.anchor: “Endâd”, “nidd”in cem‘idir. “Misil” ve “emsâl” gibi ki mânaları birdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The use of jaʿl shows that any likeness attributed to God is fabricated, not true, and therefore false.
rows.anchor: جعل (ca‘l) tâbiri gösteriyor ki Allah’a hangi şeyden olursa olsun misil tasavvur olunursa uydurma olur, hak olmaz bâtıl olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowingly setting up partners means one cannot be among the protected muttaqīn and instead becomes a stubborn unbeliever.
rows.anchor: Allah’a hangi şeyden olursa olsun misil tasavvur olunursa uydurma olur, hak olmaz bâtıl olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the universal call to worship and divine oneness, Elmalılı anticipates the objection that God's command, the messenger's prophethood, and the Qur'an's divine origin are doubtful or unknown.
rows.anchor: Buna karşı birtakım insanlar: “Evet Allah belli amma bize böyle emrettiği ve peygamber gönderdiği ve Muhammedü’l-Emîn’in peygamber ve Kur’ân’ın kelâmullah olduğu ne mâlum?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To answer doubters, God follows the call to oneness with a public challenge, presenting the Qur'an as an everlasting divine proof and miracle establishing the Messenger's prophethood.
rows.anchor: umûmî olan bu da‘vet-i tevhîd ve ubûdiyeti müte‘âkib Resûlünün nübüvvetini ve ona bahşettiği Kur’ân’ın burhân-ı ilâhî olan لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ bir mu‘cize-i ebediye olduğunu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Material, time-bound miracles have limited force beyond their time and setting and later hearers can dismiss them; people chiefly benefit from religion by following enduring, rational laws and knowledge.
rows.anchor: maddî ve zamânî olan mucizelerin kuvveti ve fâidesi umûmî değildir. Onun kuvveti bulunduğu zamana ve muhîte münhasır kalır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miracles are special divine aid in moments of distress, while guidance aims to deliver people from distress; therefore the most important miracle is eternal and of rational, scientific value: the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: Hidâyetten gaye ise ıztırardan tahlîstir. Binâen‘aleyh mucizenin en mühimi ebedî, aklî ve ilmî kıymeti hâiz olan mucizedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God assured His Messenger that no person, or all people together, can imitate the Qur'an; even the greatest writers, sages, and poets fail, and challengers have repeatedly been defeated.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân’ı hiçbir insan, hatta bütün insanlar tanzir edemezler. Bu bizzat va‘d ü ta‘ahhüd-i ilâhî tahtındadır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says challengers are defeated either because God immediately binds their capacity or because He never gave it; centuries of history confirm the Qur'an's challenge.
rows.anchor: Kur’an ile tehaddîye kalkıştıkları zaman mağlub olagelmişler, hiçbir şey yapamamışlardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı recounts Napoleon claiming to love Muhammad as a great commander but to surpass him; Napoleon's pride began to collapse at Acre and faded, while France could not heal the wounds he opened.
rows.anchor: “Ben Muhammed’i severim, o da benim gibi büyük bir kumandan idi fakat ben daha büyüğüm” demişti. Bu gururu, bu tehaddîye kıyâmı nihâyet Akka kalesinden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı concludes that the Qur'an's challenge is the eternal law and proof of both the Qur'an and Muhammad's prophethood, offered in response to human doubt.
rows.anchor: Hâsılı sırr-ı tehaddî Kur’ân’ın ve nübüvvet-i Muhammediyenin ebedî bir kanunu ve burhânıdır.
